correctness.rationale: The proof identifies the four singleton units, then forces unit-fixing automorphisms to commute with translation. It exhausts all translation orbits, separates A from C by square-to-absorber, fixes the B shift by its unique idempotent and forces C shift 2k by A+A. The full multiplication table establishes the converse; inversion conjugates K_k to K_-k. Reduced stabilizer and explicit witness are verified. The actual standalone checker tests 32 necessary candidate maps and every multiplication pair, reproducing exactly four normalized and eight total valid maps.

originality.rationale: The new claim computes the full fifteen-element power-semigroup automorphism group of C4 and its reduced-stabilizer. The 2026 source poses reduced-submonoid invariance as an open conjecture; the 2025 theorem treats the reduced monoid alone; the 2018/2021 paper treats factorization, not automorphism groups. Recorded previous exact group computations for C3 or C2×C2 do not imply the C4 result because C4 introduces a separate order-two translation orbit. Precise historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: An older finite-semigroup table or classification under different nomenclature might independently compute the same D8 group.
The exact source comparison is not an independent literature audit; absence of search matches is not proof of priority.

value.rationale: This is a complete exact automorphism-group computation for the smallest cyclic even-order group with a nontrivial proper subgroup. The B orbit creates an additional structural constraint absent from the known C3 case, producing a distinct D8 group. It locates exactly which full-power symmetries fail to preserve the reduced monoid in a recently motivated rigidity problem. It is naturally classifying the complete smallest new case, not an arbitrary selected parameter.
